pharm: Non-iodinated benzofuran with antiarrhythmic actions of all four Vaughan-Williams classes; reduces atrial-fibrillation-related hospitalisation in patients in sinus rhythm
quick: 400 mg twice daily, one tablet with the morning and one with the evening meal
Take with food; avoid grapefruit juice
May cause fetal harm (animal malformations); confirm not pregnant, use contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 5 days after treatment
Monitor renal function (small creatinine rise expected); no initial dose change
Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment; discontinue if hepatic injury suspected
ECG/rhythm every 3 months, QT, LFTs, renal function, potassium/magnesium, HF signs
summary: Dronedarone (Multaq) is an oral non-iodinated benzofuran antiarrhythmic, structurally related to amiodarone, indicated to reduce the risk of hospitalisation for atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients in sinus rhythm with a history of paroxysmal or persistent AF. The dose is 400 mg twice daily taken with the morning and evening meals. It has antiarrhythmic properties spanning all four Vaughan-Williams classes. It carries a BOXED WARNING: it is contraindicated in symptomatic heart failure with recent decompensation requiring hospitalisation or NYHA Class IV heart failure (it doubles the risk of death), and in PERMANENT AF (patients who cannot or will not be cardioverted to sinus rhythm) where it doubles the risk of death, stroke and heart-failure hospitalisation. Cardiac rhythm must be checked at least every 3 months and patients cardioverted or the drug stopped if AF recurs. Other risks include hepatotoxicity, pulmonary toxicity, QT prolongation, and embryofetal toxicity. It is a moderate CYP3A and CYP2D6 inhibitor with numerous important drug interactions (digoxin, statins, dabigatran, QT-prolonging drugs).
indications: To reduce the risk of hospitalisation for atrial fibrillation in patients in sinus rhythm with a history of paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation

dosage.t: One tablet with the morning meal and one with the evening meal
dosage.n: Stop Class I/III antiarrhythmics and strong CYP3A inhibitors before starting; verify not pregnant

dosage.d: Ensure patient is in sinus rhythm and on appropriate antithrombotic therapy
dosage.n: Contraindicated in permanent AF and recently decompensated/Class IV heart failure

dosage.d: Continue 400 mg twice daily; reassess rhythm at least every 3 months
dosage.n: If AF recurs, cardiovert or discontinue; no dose reduction in mild-moderate hepatic/renal impairment

admin: Take one 400 mg tablet with the morning meal and one with the evening meal
Stop treatment with Class I or III antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, flecainide, propafenone, quinidine, disopyramide, dofetilide, sotalol) and strong CYP3A inhibitors before starting
Verify that females of reproductive potential are not pregnant before initiation and ensure effective contraception
Do not take with grapefruit juice (raises dronedarone levels)
Ensure appropriate antithrombotic (anticoagulant) therapy before and throughout treatment
Determine cardiac rhythm at least every 3 months; if AF is detected, cardiovert or discontinue
moa: The precise mechanism of dronedarone is unknown. It is a non-iodinated benzofuran derivative (structurally related to amiodarone but without the iodine moiety) that exhibits antiarrhythmic properties of all four Vaughan-Williams classes: it blocks sodium channels (Class I), has non-competitive antiadrenergic activity (Class II), blocks potassium channels prolonging repolarisation (Class III), and blocks calcium channels (Class IV). These actions slow heart rate, prolong atrial and AV-nodal conduction and refractoriness, and produce concentration-dependent increases in PR and QTc intervals, helping maintain sinus rhythm and reduce AF-related hospitalisation.

absolute: Permanent atrial fibrillation (cannot or will not be cardioverted to sinus rhythm)
Symptomatic heart failure with recent decompensation requiring hospitalisation, or NYHA Class IV heart failure
Second- or third-degree AV block or sick sinus syndrome (without a functioning pacemaker)
Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, cyclosporine, telithromycin, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir) or erythromycin
Concomitant drugs/herbal products prolonging QT and risking torsades de pointes
Liver or lung toxicity related to previous amiodarone use
QTc interval over 500 ms or PR interval over 280 ms
Hypersensitivity to dronedarone or any excipient
relative: Concomitant beta-blockers or calcium-channel blockers (additive bradycardia/AV block - start low)
Concurrent digoxin, dabigatran, statins or other CYP3A/P-gp substrates
monitor: Cardiac rhythm at least every 3 months
ECG QT/PR intervals and heart rate
Renal function (expect a small reversible creatinine rise)
Signs/symptoms of heart failure and pulmonary toxicity

preg: Dronedarone may cause fetal harm: in animal studies it produced multiple visceral and skeletal malformations at doses at or below the maximum recommended human dose. There are no adequate human data. It is contraindicated in pregnancy; verify that females of reproductive potential are not pregnant before starting and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 5 days after the final dose.
lact: There are no data on dronedarone in human milk; it is present in the milk of lactating animals. Women should not breastfeed during treatment and for 5 days after the final dose.
renal: Dronedarone causes a small, early, reversible rise in serum creatinine (by partial inhibition of tubular creatinine secretion) that does not reflect reduced glomerular filtration. No initial dose adjustment is required, but renal function should be monitored periodically, and a marked sustained rise should prompt further evaluation.
hepatic: Dronedarone is extensively metabolised by the liver and can cause hepatocellular liver injury, including rare cases of acute liver failure requiring transplantation. It is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver enzymes (especially in the first 6 months) and discontinue if significant hepatic injury is suspected.

major: Class I or III antiarrhythmics and other QT-prolonging drugs (phenothiazines, tricyclics, certain macrolides) - contraindicated; risk of torsades de pointes
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, etc.) and erythromycin - contraindicated; markedly increase dronedarone levels

Digoxin - dronedarone raises digoxin levels and potentiates its electrophysiologic effects; discontinue or halve digoxin dose and monitor (increased arrhythmic/sudden-death risk noted with concurrent digoxin)
Simvastatin/other CYP3A and P-gp statins - increased myopathy risk; limit simvastatin to 10 mg/day
Dabigatran and other P-gp substrates - increased exposure
moderate: Beta-blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers - additive bradycardia/AV block; start at low dose and uptitrate after ECG
CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic index (sirolimus, tacrolimus) - monitor and adjust
Warfarin - monitor INR after starting dronedarone
minor: CYP3A inducers (rifampicin, phenytoin, St John's wort) - reduce dronedarone efficacy; avoid
interactions.food: Take with meals (improves bioavailability); avoid grapefruit juice which raises levels
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; avoid excessive intake
interactions.diagnostics: Causes a small reversible rise in serum creatinine; prolongs PR and QTc on ECG; monitor LFTs

common: Diarrhoea, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, dyspepsia
Small reversible rise in serum creatinine
serious: New onset or worsening heart failure
Hepatocellular liver injury, including rare acute liver failure
QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
Increased risk of death, stroke and HF in permanent AF or decompensated/Class IV HF (boxed warning)
emergency: Acute decompensated heart failure or pulmonary oedema
Acute liver failure (jaundice, dark urine, severe fatigue)

monitoring: Cardiac rhythm at least every 3 months; cardiovert or discontinue if AF recurs
ECG QT and PR intervals, heart rate
Liver aminotransferases at baseline and periodically (especially first 6 months)
Serum potassium and magnesium (correct before and during therapy)
Signs and symptoms of heart failure and pulmonary toxicity; ensure ongoing antithrombotic therapy
counsel: Take one tablet with your morning meal and one with your evening meal, and avoid grapefruit juice
Report acute weight gain, swelling, or worsening breathlessness - these may signal heart failure
Report loss of appetite, nausea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or severe tiredness - signs of liver injury
Keep taking your blood-thinning medicine and attend regular ECG and blood-test checks
Tell your doctor about all medicines you take - dronedarone interacts with many drugs
Use effective contraception; do not use if pregnant and do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Steady state reached within 4 to 8 days of twice-daily dosing
Peak plasma concentration about 3 to 6 hours after dosing (fed)
Maintained with twice-daily dosing; low oral bioavailability (~15% with food)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: contraindicated and doubles mortality in recently decompensated/NYHA Class IV heart failure and in permanent AF (also doubles stroke and HF hospitalisation in permanent AF)
Only for patients in sinus rhythm with paroxysmal/persistent AF - check rhythm at least every 3 months
Non-iodinated amiodarone analogue - fewer thyroid/pulmonary effects than amiodarone but less efficacious
Causes a benign reversible rise in serum creatinine (inhibits tubular secretion, not true GFR fall)
Many interactions: contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors and QT-prolonging drugs; halve digoxin; limit simvastatin to 10 mg
Take with food and avoid grapefruit juice; ensure ongoing anticoagulation
missed: If you miss a dose, take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time - do not take a double dose to make up for the missed one. Consult your doctor before stopping treatment.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In overdose, monitor the patient's cardiac rhythm and blood pressure and provide supportive, symptom-based treatment. It is unknown whether dronedarone or its metabolites are removed by dialysis.
